questions.prompt: You build a Smart List filtered by Owner = Your Name and you're seeing half the leads you expected. What's almost certainly wrong?
choices: Your pipeline stage filter is too narrow.
You need to add Follower = Your Name with OR logic — legacy leads where you're the follower (not owner) don't show up otherwise, and without both you'll miss half your book.
The location filter is excluding some leads.
You need to clear your browser cache.
questions.explanation: The Owner+Follower rule is explicit: set both, leave logic as OR. Without both filters you'll miss half your book — this is how leads go missing and other reps close your sales. The fix is always the follower filter, not a cache clear.

questions.prompt: You just live-dialed 10 leads and got no answer. It's 4:55 PM. What's the right play — and what should you absolutely not do?
choices: Leave manual voicemails on all 10 for maximum coverage.
Redial each one three more times before logging off.
Leave them for tomorrow's power-dial session.
Fire an end-of-day VM drop workflow, optionally paired with a follow-up SMS, and never leave a manual VM — missed calls without VMs get returned more often than missed calls with them.
questions.explanation: The critical rule is 'never leave a voicemail manually' — only scheduled VM drops go out, and they batch at end of day. Manual VMs tank callback rates. Redialing burns the lead; deferring violates the speed-to-lead principle.

questions.prompt: A lead texts 'are you a bot?' mid-conversation. What's the canonical transparency script?
choices: 'No, I'm a real person.'

'Yes — we use AI to help manage text volume. We have over 300 people texting us on a daily basis right now and we couldn't get back to everyone in a timely manner without it. But I'm a real person when you call.'
'That's a weird question.'
Ignore the question and move on to pricing.
questions.explanation: The transparency script frames busy-ness as proof the brand is wanted — status-raising disclosure, not defensive. Lying about the bot destroys trust when they catch you; ignoring the question signals guilt. 'We're busy because we're in demand' is the lift.

questions.prompt: You want to VM-drop 150 leads before lunch. What's the operational rule?
choices: Drop all 150 at once so you're done.
Drop 50 now and 100 tomorrow.
Drip in batches of 20 every 5 minutes — drop 100+ at once and you'll get 20 callbacks in five minutes that you can't answer all of.
Never drop more than 10 at a time.
questions.explanation: Drip mode exists for exactly this reason — a 150-drop all at once generates a wave of simultaneous callbacks that one rep can't handle, burning the leads who get voicemail instead of you. 20 every 5 minutes is the module-specified cadence.

questions.prompt: A lead is in the CALL SCHEDULED stage. Which of these actions is explicitly forbidden?
choices: Updating their contact notes.
Texting them a confirmation the morning of.
Power-dialing them as part of a daily blitz — they have a booked time, calling twice is rude, and all automations pause at this stage.
Logging a no-show disposition after the call.
questions.explanation: The module says don't power-dial CALL SCHEDULED leads — they have a booked time; calling twice is rude. VM drops are also forbidden here. Automations pause at this stage on purpose — the human-only interaction is the scheduled call itself.

questions.prompt: It's Friday afternoon. Your Close Won count for the week is 14. What's the sale-audit rule?
choices: Celebrate — GHL is the source of truth.
Ask your pod leader to audit for you.

Cross-reference every Close Won against the POS system — if you moved a lead to Close Won but never pressed 'Confirm' on the agreement in the POS, you created a ghost sale. No payment actually processed. Reach back out immediately on any mismatch.
Audit only the highest-priced sales.
questions.explanation: The weekly Friday sale-audit catches ghost sales — where GHL says Close Won but no payment processed in the POS. Every Close Won gets cross-referenced. Skipping the audit or auditing selectively means unpaid sales on your commission sheet and a refund situation when the lead never gets charged.

questions.prompt: A lead's conversation with the Conversation AI bot has gone off-rail — it quoted a wrong price. What's the correct intervention?
choices: Escalate to engineering to fix the bot globally.
Delete the conversation.
Move the lead to Close Lost.
Click the sparkle icon in the lead's text screen, set the bot to Inactive for that lead, and correct the conversation yourself. Skim your book at least twice a day to catch this proactively.
questions.explanation: You are still the owner — the bot doesn't replace rep attention. Skim text threads at least twice a day, and when the bot goes off-brand/off-pricing/off-tone, turn it off for that lead via the sparkle icon and correct. Deleting the thread or close-losting the lead destroys a fixable situation.

questions.prompt: You want to send a one-off price snippet but the lead just asked a specific question you haven't addressed. What's the rule?
choices: Slow down and type a custom response — a wrong-snippet send is worse than no snippet. Always scan the context before sending.
Fire the snippet anyway — snippets save time.
Fire two snippets to cover more ground.
Send the snippet and then type a follow-up.
questions.explanation: A wrong-snippet send is explicitly worse than no snippet — it signals you weren't actually reading. Always scan context first. Snippets are for consistent repeatable sends (pricing recap, grace-period explainer); they're not a substitute for attention to the actual conversation.

questions.prompt: You're about to send a text and GHL offers to dial/text from a local-area-code number matching the lead's. What's the recommended move and why?
choices: Always use your original number for consistency.
Only use local numbers for Close Won follow-ups.
Ask your pod leader each time before choosing.
Use the local number whenever available — local numbers get 2–3x higher answer rates than out-of-area numbers.
questions.explanation: Local-area-code numbers get 2–3x higher answer rates — always use when available. The consistency argument works against you here: strangers-area-code = ignored call. Asking pod leader every time is a waste of their time on a rule-driven decision.

questions.prompt: A new rep asks if she should build her own workflow to automate a rehash campaign she has in mind. What's the rule?
choices: Go ahead — experimentation is encouraged.
Do not build your own automations without pod leader approval — broken workflows can text the entire list, and Sub-Account settings are off-limits unless explicitly instructed.
Build it in a test account first.
Use the Admin tab — it's safer.
questions.explanation: The 'what not to do in GHL' section is explicit: no DIY automations without pod leader approval, don't send mass texts without a filter, don't touch Sub-Account settings or Admin tabs. A broken workflow can text every lead in the sub-account. When in doubt, ask.
